text:
A: Hi, can you hear me okay?
B: Yes, hello. I am Tomasz, Warrington.
A: Gareth, Chelmsford. Nice to meet you, Tomasz. Is that a Polish name?
B: Yes. I am from near Rzeszów, south-east. I came here in 2007.
A: Oh, nice. I've done Kraków a couple of times, but never that far east. Is it worth going?
B: For me, yes, my mother is there. For tourist, er, I don't know. It is small town. Quiet.
A: Quiet's underrated, to be honest. What do you do?
B: I am student. Civil engineering, Salford, second year. I am forty-four, so I am the old one.
A: Fair play. Did you do something before that?
B: Eleven years in warehouse, shift supervisor. Rotas, deliveries.
A: Right. I did Geography at Leicester, ages ago, and then sort of fell into travel. I'm a travel consultant now, tailor-made trips, mostly Japan and Asia. Long term, I'd like to set up on my own, so I've been building up a client list, working out the numbers. It's the same instinct as yours, I think. Get the qualification, get the plan, then make the jump, yeah?
B: Maybe. For me, the plan is simple. Finish in 2026, get graduate job, maybe council, buy a house again.
A: That's a good plan, though. Clear. Do you get away at all, between terms?
B: Every August I go to my mother, two, three weeks. That is all.
A: You should do Croatia sometime. Split, then the islands. Off-season, it's brilliant value, and the food's...
B: We went to Croatia, my wife and me. Before.
A: Oh, right. Did you like it?
B: Yes. Very much. She died, in 2021. Since then I don't go anywhere, really. Only to my mother.
A: I'm really sorry, Tomasz. I didn't mean to put my foot in it.
B: No, it is okay. You didn't know.
A: Have you got kids?
B: One son, Kacper, fourteen. We live with my brother now, and his wife. It is good for Kacper, family after school.
A: That makes a lot of sense. Is he into engineering as well?
B: Not yet. Football, phone. I help him with maths homework, he says I explain it the Polish way.
A: Ha. What's the Polish way?
B: Longer. With more shouting, he says. It is not true.
A: What do you do to switch off? I run, mostly. Marathon training, along the towpath.
B: I walk. Every evening, Sankey Valley trail. Not running. My knees say no.
A: Walking's good. I log mine on Strava, which is probably a bit sad.
B: I have spreadsheet of my university marks, so I cannot say anything.
A: Ha. We'd get on, then. What's the hardest module this...
